A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AutoToM and provide readable main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A1–A6. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V2 reports original benchmark evaluations, comparisons of model predictions with human judgments, ablations, and embodied-assistance simulations.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and adds FANToM, OpenToM, alternative-backend, efficiency, and repeated-run evaluations.

M1.justification: Appendix A3.3.2 explicitly extends the causal structure with attitude and preference for OpenToM, keeping other components unchanged. The core Bayesian inverse planning, agent-model discovery, and online SMC procedures are retained.

E1.justification: V3 adds conversational false-belief inference on FANToM and affective attitude inference on OpenToM. These substantially broaden the represented situations and mental-state tasks beyond the five retained benchmarks, cognitive studies, and household assistance scenarios.

E2.justification: New Table 2 evaluates standalone Qwen3-235B, DeepSeek-V3, and Gemini-2.5-Flash against AutoToM using their respective backends. Table 1 retains its comparator set. Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking disappears from the main cognitive-study table but remains evaluated in Appendix Figure A3.

E3.justification: Added protocols specify 200 randomly selected short-context, first-order false-belief FANToM questions and all 596 OpenToM attitude questions, evaluated using Macro-F1. The MMToM-QA backend study holds prompts fixed and disables Gemini-2.5-Flash thinking. Existing benchmark and assistance protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.1 adds a sensitivity study testing dependence on the LLM backend on MMToM-QA. Existing component ablations, scalability analyses, and qualitative cases are retained. New Figure A2 elaborates an existing inference example rather than introducing a separate case study.

E5.justification: V3 explicitly reports additional MMToM-QA trials across three random seeds: AutoToM achieves 82.56% mean accuracy with 0.45% standard error, and o3-mini-high achieves 65.94% with 0.59% standard error. V2 already reports cognitive-study significance and O-WAH repeated runs with standard errors.

E6.justification: V3 substantially extends the quantitative findings while retaining Table 1 and the original ablation scores. New results include FANToM accuracy of 72.7% for AutoToM with GPT-4o versus 57.5% for GPT-4o, and OpenToM Macro-F1 of 0.56 versus GPT-4o's 0.48 and o3-mini-high's 0.60. Backend comparisons, token/runtime measurements, and repeated-run estimates are also added.

T1.justification: The Bayesian inference equations, utility definition, recursive-state formulation, model-space discussion, and SMC mathematics are retained. Figure A2 numerically illustrates the existing inference calculation; it does not introduce a new theoretical result or revise the formal reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: automated agent modeling, scalable Bayesian mental inference, strong benchmark performance, human-like confidence estimates, and embodied assistance. The added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations concerning conversational observation tracking and why OpenToM attitude inference can use forward estimation without inverse planning. A3.6 also adds an overbroad claim of state-of-the-art results across all benchmarks, despite contrary comparisons such as Hi-ToM's 72.5% versus o3-mini-high's 75.0%. Existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 supplies identifiers and configuration information for the additional backends. Appendix A4.2 newly states that GPT-4o and o3-mini-high received the same rationality-assumption instruction; this disclosure does not establish a rerun of the existing cognitive experiments. Core prompts, hyperparameters, and project/code links are unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations to SoMi-ToM, FANToM, OpenToM, and work on reinforcement learning from user conversations. Section 2 expands its comparison with already-cited thought-tracing, emphasizing causal models and adaptive complexity, and removes the assertion that AutoToM requires no domain-specific knowledge or implementations.

P1.justification: V3 adds focused explanatory paragraphs and experimental subsections, reorganizes Appendix A3, makes limited language edits, and replaces the date header with the conference designation. Most existing prose and the overall section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds the backend comparison table, token/runtime table, and detailed inference Figure A2. It relocates existing displays and reformats the benchmark summary. The main cognitive table loses its Gemini column, while the corresponding appendix scatterplots remain. Most existing figures and tables retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: The new backend and seed checks strengthen reliability evidence, while additional tasks and efficiency comparisons improve assessment of applicability and computational cost. These are incremental gains over v2's extensive existing evaluation. The new blanket state-of-the-art statement in A3.6 overstates the reported comparisons, but this limited reporting weakness does not outweigh the added validation.
